card.title: House IPA
card.purpose: The finite house inventory is the shared notation and feature space into which the library reads other phone spellings.
card.conventions: Registered entries use the library's IPA spelling, tie, boundary, and prosody conventions; inventory order is declaration order.
card.strengths: Use it when a finite, feature-bearing reference inventory and an identity spelling boundary are wanted.
card.limitations: It is a declared working inventory rather than a claim that every possible or attested IPA segment is registered.

note.origin: CONTRIBUTING.md: Registered wins; composition is the fallback

card.note: Registered sounds become candidates for inventory search and models; a well-formed unregistered tie chain can still compose without being promoted into the finite inventory.

card.title: Wild IPA
card.purpose: The soft reader brings common external IPA-like spellings into house IPA when a caller explicitly asks for forgiving input.
card.conventions: It applies declared lookalikes and then requires a strict house-IPA result; spelling remains house IPA.
card.strengths: Use it at an import boundary where keyboard substitutes and canonically equivalent spellings are expected.
card.limitations: It has no finite phoneset, so it is a notation style rather than a reference inventory for mapping or distance.
card.note: Soft lookalikes are read only through explicit wild import, leaving strict house parsing unchanged.

card.title: CMUdict
card.purpose: The CMUdict style reads and spells the ARPAbet vocabulary used by pronunciation dictionaries for speech synthesis and lexical work.
card.conventions: Vowel stress digits are meaningful: primary, secondary, and unstressed spellings remain distinct house units where the dictionary distinguishes them.
card.strengths: Use it for CMUdict-format lexicons whose stress markings should survive inventory derivation and round trips.
card.limitations: The mapping is an explicit finite ARPAbet boundary, not a general parser for arbitrary ASCII phonetic notation.
card.note: `AH0` and `AH1` read as distinct house units, preserving the stress contrast the dictionary writes.

card.title: PocketSphinx
card.purpose: The PocketSphinx style presents the CMU phone vocabulary under the stressless convention expected by recognizer dictionaries.
card.conventions: It shares the declared CMU phone map while refusing stress digits and recognizing the style's silence and boundary labels.
card.strengths: Use it for stressless PocketSphinx lexicons where accepting a stress-bearing token would overstate what the notation commits to.
card.limitations: It intentionally does not repair a CMUdict pronunciation by stripping stress; the `cmudict` style is the appropriate reader when digits carry information.
card.note: Stress digits are refused rather than silently discarded, so a dictionary in the neighboring convention fails clearly.

card.title: TIMIT
card.purpose: The TIMIT style reads and spells the corpus's acoustic-phonetic segment labels in house IPA.
card.conventions: Main labels provide canonical spellings; closure, epenthetic, syllabic, and pause labels are accepted as declared extras without replacing the canonical choice.
card.strengths: Use it for TIMIT label interchange and for a finite sound inventory in the corpus's transcription convention.
card.limitations: Several corpus labels can describe the same house sound or structural material, so label count and finite phone count answer different questions.
card.note: The declaration retains closure and pause labels for corpus interchange, while the inventory applies the shared silence rule and counts sounds.

card.title: eSpeak NG
card.purpose: The language-scoped inventories expose eSpeak NG's compact synthesis phoneme tables, and the family union supplies the vocabulary emitted by eSpeak-based recognizers.
card.conventions: Each language resolves eSpeak table inheritance into native mnemonics; the union reads a mnemonic only where every declaration carrying it agrees on one house phone.
card.strengths: Use a language member for synthesis-facing text in that table's convention, or the union for cross-language recognizer vocabulary coverage.
card.limitations: A shared mnemonic can mean different sounds in different language tables, so the union deliberately refuses an ambiguous read or spelling instead of choosing one language silently.
card.note: The union ranks agreed spellings by declaration coverage, length, and lexical order; selecting `espeak:<code>` retains a language table's own answer where tables disagree.

card.title: Montreal Forced Aligner
card.purpose: The language and variety members carry the phone sets of freely shared MFA pronunciation dictionaries, while the union provides a broad aligner-facing vocabulary.
card.conventions: Dictionary tokens are segmented; each declared MFA phone becomes one house unit, with ties added when one MFA token is written by several IPA characters.
card.strengths: Use a language member with its matching aligner dictionary, and derive an attested inventory from a dictionary when token or entry weight matters.
card.limitations: The family union combines doculects, while a declared member records membership rather than how broadly each phone is attested in its dictionary.
card.note: In the pinned en-US dictionary, the smallest frequency-ranked prefix reaching 99% of `{mfa_en_us_tokens:,}` phone tokens contains `{mfa_en_us_core_99}` of `{mfa_en_us_types}` phones.

The low-attestation tail contains xenophones in loans and names, including `pʷ` in `{p_labialized_entries}` entries and `ɡʷ` in `{g_labialized_entries}`, alongside ordinary English allophony written for few eligible words; an entry cutoff locates this tail but cannot interpret it.

`ɱ` occurs in `{labiodental_nasal_entries}` dictionary entry and `{labiodental_nasal_tokens}` token, as an alternate for *infection*; it is labiodental assimilation, not a xenophone. Recording that assimilation for one word is a reasonable lexicographic judgment, while its rarity measures how often the variant was written rather than whether English has the sound.

The `{mfa_en_us_placeholders}` marker-only entries — `{mfa_en_us_placeholder_names}` — serve the aligner rather than pronounce words, so dictionary ingestion excludes them from phone counts and reports each one.

card.title: Panphon (development comparison)
card.purpose: The dev-only declaration is a comparison target for running Panphon's feature geometry through the same declared machinery as the house system.
card.conventions: Its generated table preserves Panphon's ternary feature values, source spelling normalization, weight order, and declared round-trip losses without promoting it to a shipped style or inventory.
card.strengths: Use it to compare feature systems and cost policies on common inputs while keeping Panphon's own data visible and reproducible.
card.limitations: It is a compatibility target rather than a correctness oracle: unsupported segments can be dropped by Panphon, and a ternary zero does not distinguish several kinds of underspecification.
card.note: The declaration contains `{panphon_segments}` segment rows over `{panphon_features}` features and `{panphon_weights}` supplied weights; generation normalizes every segment key to NFD and refuses a duplicate normalized key.
Feature and weight order differ at the tail, and the generated declaration retains that order instead of quietly repairing the comparison target.
